source_metadata.title: Non-toxigenic penicillin-resistant cutaneous C. diphtheriae infection: A case report and review of the literature
source_metadata.journal: Journal of Infection and Public Health

source_integrity_review.source_text_issue: The susceptibility sentence on page 99 is grammatically incomplete ("were penicillin and sensitive to erythromycin"); penicillin resistance is supported independently by the article title, Summary, and author conclusions.

semantic_spot_checks.claim: Index patient was a previously healthy 14-year-old girl with travel to Ethiopia and ulcerated lower-extremity lesions.
Reference laboratory confirmed non-toxigenic C. diphtheriae by PCR and ELEK testing.
Article presents the isolate as penicillin resistant and erythromycin sensitive.
Erythromycin caused nausea/vomiting and was replaced after one day by azithromycin.
No main-text figures or tables are present.

extraction_limitations: Single-patient case report; no controlled efficacy comparison or resistance prevalence estimate is supported.
The narrative review summarizes six cited sources; those secondary summaries were tagged secondary_reported_result and not treated as primary-study evidence.
No MIC values or detailed susceptibility testing method are reported in the supplied article.
The source contains the incomplete susceptibility phrase noted above; no missing word was invented.
schema_gaps: The current atom model has no dedicated case-report event/clinical-course atom kind; descriptive clinical events are represented as qualitative_result or other.

Secondary quantitative literature-review summaries cannot be cleanly normalized as quantitative_result without inventing exposure/outcome structure, so they remain other atoms with secondary_reported_result tags.
